gap: No result ChatGPT got states that macOS does not support DisplayPort MST for extended displays, so one native USB-C video cable can only carry one extended screen to a Mac. On an M4 or M5 MacBook Air, a driver-free triple extender therefore needs both Thunderbolt ports, one per screen, with MagSafe left for charging. For the same reason, Xebec says the single-cable Tri-Screen 3 needs its DisplayLink Mac Adapter on every Mac, not only on M1, M2 and M3 models.
standout_why: I opened Macworld's 'How to connect multiple monitors to MacBooks' guide (cited in 4 chats) and Plugable's KB article 'Understanding External Display Support on Apple M1…M5' (cited). Neither mentions MST, and neither says that a single-cable extender mirrors or needs a driver even on an M4 or M5. Macworld covers the DisplayLink HDCP and Screen Recording limits. That part is already taken. Plugable's 'Apple Silicon Macs and Plugable Products' page, cited in one chat, was not opened because of my tool budget, so it may carry part of this. ChatGPT's answers say 'M1/M2/M3 users need the separate DisplayLink Mac adapter' for the Xebec, which Xebec's help center contradicts. Our current page also lacks the MST reason and the all-Macs adapter requirement for the Xebec.
decides: It confirms the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro as the pick for an M4 or M5 Air. Its two USB-C cables, one per screen, drive both screens natively with no driver: Macworld's Simon Jary says Macs above plain M1 and M2 run both screens 'without the software download', and Apple specs two external displays plus the built-in screen. The Xebec Tri-Screen 3 runs on a single cable, so it stays tied to the $59 DisplayLink adapter and its driver even on an M5 Air. That makes it a weaker buy for new Airs and moves it to the 'M1–M3 or must-be-one-cable' slot. On M1, M2 and M3 Airs every candidate needs a driver either way, so the finding doesn't change the pick there.

findings.label: macOS support for DisplayPort MST (one cable driving two extended screens)
findings.value: Not supported; an MST hub on a Mac, even an M5 Max, mirrors the same image on both monitors
findings.source_title: Understanding Multiple Displays on Apple Silicon Macs – Plugable
findings.note: Plugable article dated 2026-03-06: 'macOS still does not support MST for extended displays'; its FAQ says macOS 'will only "mirror" the display' with MST. It adds that two independent screens from one cable need 'a Thunderbolt or DisplayLink docking station'. This is Plugable's statement. I found no Apple support page that says it.

findings.label: Plugable on DisplayLink for base M1/M2/M3 Macs
findings.value: DisplayLink is 'the only way to get dual or triple displays on the new MacBook Neo or the base M1/M2/M3 models'
findings.source_title: Understanding Multiple Displays on Apple Silicon Macs – Plugable
findings.note: Same article. Its FAQ also says the base M5 in the 2026 MacBook Air 'natively supports two external displays while the laptop's built-in screen remains active'.

findings.label: MacBook Air (M5) external displays and ports
findings.value: Up to two external displays (6K 60 Hz or 4K 144 Hz each) while the built-in display runs at full native resolution; two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports plus a MagSafe 3 charging port
findings.source_title: MacBook Air 13- and 15-inch (M5) - Tech Specs - Apple
findings.note: Same for 13-inch and 15-inch. Because MST isn't supported, the two native extended screens take one Thunderbolt port each. That leaves no free USB-C port and leaves MagSafe for charging. That conclusion is my reading of the two sourced facts, not Apple's wording.

findings.label: MacBook Air 13-inch (M4, 2025) external displays and ports
findings.value: Up to two external displays up to 6K 60 Hz at the same time as the built-in display at full native resolution; native DisplayPort 1.4 over USB-C; two Thunderbolt 4 ports plus MagSafe 3
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: Mac requirement
findings.value: The Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter is required on every Mac; Xebec lists 'Mac USB-C only' as 'Not compatible — Mac Adapter required'
findings.source_title: Which USB-C Ports Are Compatible with the Tri-Screen 3 and Dual-Screen 3? – Xebec Help Center
findings.note: Xebec's reason: 'The Tri-Screen 3 drives two external screens at the same time, which requires more than a standard USB-C DisplayPort connection can handle on a Mac.' Xebec's Dual-Screen 3, which has one screen, works from a capable port with no adapter. Xebec does not exempt M4 or M5 Macs. The page shows only 'Updated 3 months ago'. A search snippet says the adapter is a DisplayLink device, but I could not open the adapter page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: How it connects to a Mac without the driver
findings.value: Two included USB-C cables, one per screen; Macs above plain M1 and M2 can run both screens without the software download; plain M1 and M2 Macs need Mobile Pixels' free driver ('rather like DisplayLink')
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Macworld's Simon Jary also writes that the screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'. Full brightness needs a power adapter on one of the Trio's USB-C ports. On an M4 or M5 Air the two screen cables take both Thunderbolt ports, so that adapter is the only way to reach full brightness. Macworld lists the price as $499.99.

findings.label: Mac driver
findings.value: Separate macOS downloads for macOS 14 and later (v4.1.0), 13/12/11, 10.15 and 10.14–10.9; maker warns 'DO NOT plug the Mobile Pixels Inc Device into your mac before executing the driver installation'
findings.source_title: 2023 Trio Series: Mac Display Driver – Mobile Pixels
findings.note: The page covers Trio Series 2nd and 3rd Gen. It does not say what the driver enables, such as single-cable dual extended mode.

findings.label: DisplayLink limits on macOS (already in a cited rival)
findings.value: Once one DisplayLink screen is connected, protected (HDCP) content becomes unavailable on all screens; the Screen Recording permission must be enabled
findings.source_title: How to connect multiple monitors to MacBooks (M1, M2, M3, M4 & M5) – Macworld
findings.note: Macworld's guide is cited by ChatGPT, so this is not new. It matters for the Xebec on every Mac, and for the Trio 3 Pro only on M1, M2 and M3 Airs or in one-cable mode.

unsourced: An Apple-authored statement that macOS doesn't support DisplayPort MST. I searched support.apple.com and found only Apple Community threads; the 'How many displays' article (support.apple.com/en-us/101571) doesn't cover MST.
Xebec Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter page (price, DisplayLink wording, M4/M5 listing): thexebec.com, europe.thexebec.com and storecheck all returned HTTP 429.

Mobile Pixels' own statement on what the Trio 3 Pro does over one cable on a Mac without the driver (mirror or one screen): mobilepixels.us/products/trio returned HTTP 429, and the 2023 Trio manual PDF was over 10 MB and didn't load.

Whether the UPERFECT Z 14 Tri Screen, INVZI MagHub Trio Go 16 and KEFEYA S2Pro use MST or a USB-graphics chip in single-cable mode: the uperfectmonitor.com store returned HTTP 429, and I ran out of tool budget for INVZI and KEFEYA.
